text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- State (central) Bank of Pakistan governor Muhammad Yaqub said discussions with the International Monetary Fund focused on how to make a transition to an Extended Structural Adjustment Facility/Extended Fund Facility and ended on a positive note.
- Leaders of 54 Islamic states are meeting in Islamabad Sunday to consider the global challenges confronting Moslems in the 21st century and devise ways to overcome them.
- A deputy of Punjab provincial assembly from Lahore was shot dead and four other people were wounded on Saturday.
- The import bill of petroleum products will leap to $5 billion in three years from $2 billion in 1995/96 (July-June).
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the IMF has agreed in principle to give a three-year package to Pakistan after the announcement of the structural reforms programmes.
- The Karachi Electric Supply Corp is likely to be privatised in the next three months.
- The latest agreement with the International Monetary Fund to enter into Extended Structural Adjustment Facility will save Pakistan additional taxation of 25 billion rupees.
- Hectic efforts are being made by Pakistani authorities to seek the release of 37 men of the Anti-Narcotics Force led by a senior officer who were held in neighbouring Afghanistan.

- Iranian deputy foreign minister Alaeddin Boroujerdi said no single Afghan group could rule Afghanistan by imposing its military will and proposed that Iran and Pakistan draw up a joint strategy to solve the Afghan conflict.
